evals.prompt: I'm inside a Herdr session (HERDR_ENV=1 is set, I'm in pane 1-2). I want to spawn a second Claude instance in a new pane to review the test coverage in src/api/ while I keep working here. How do I do that?
evals.expected_output: Use herdr agent start to spawn a named agent, then herdr agent send to give it the task — keeping focus on the current pane throughout
assertions: Response uses herdr agent start to spawn the new Claude instance (preferred over pane split for named agents)
Response gives the new agent a name/label so it can be addressed by name afterward
Response keeps focus on the current pane (uses --no-focus default or explicitly avoids --focus)
Response shows how to send the review task to the new agent (herdr agent send or herdr pane run)
Response does NOT use sleep as a waiting mechanism

evals.prompt: I've got two agents running in my Herdr session. The codex agent in pane 1-1 is refactoring the auth module and will exit when done. I need to wait for it to finish, then read what it did, and only then start my own work on the tests. Show me the commands.
evals.expected_output: herdr wait agent-status with --status done (not idle, since codex exits), followed by herdr pane read with --source recent-unwrapped for clean output
assertions: Response uses --status done (not idle) because the prompt says codex will exit when done
Response includes a --timeout flag on the wait command
Response uses herdr pane read with --source recent-unwrapped (not just recent) to get clean output for reading
Response explains or implies the done vs idle distinction
Response does NOT suggest polling in a loop or using sleep

evals.prompt: How do I use Herdr to run my test suite in a separate pane while keeping my Claude session focused?
evals.expected_output: Skill checks HERDR_ENV, notes the guard, still provides the correct commands with --no-focus and proper pane ID parsing from JSON
assertions: Response mentions HERDR_ENV or the guard condition (not running inside Herdr)
Response does NOT silently provide commands as if they will definitely work in the current context
Response provides the correct herdr pane split command with --no-focus
Response shows parsing the new pane ID from the JSON output (python3 or jq), not hardcoding it
